methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: For every binary 4-by-3 K, compare the exact unit-XOR minimum for the complete dirty boundary (h,y)->(h,y+Kh), with and without helper<-target feedback; three helpers, four targets, no extra registers.
scope_change_reason: PR1194 and PR1311 already address the original H2/K substitution question. Follow the explicit PR1306 next question on the adjacent D-local H1 feedback relaxation, increasing the finite domain to three helpers and four targets.
bottleneck_link: A prerequisite/negative result: D-local target feedback cannot improve scalar cost in this complete seven-register domain. No paid recursive profile or supplier changes; scalar savings would still need full physical accounting.
stop_rule: Stop after 30 minutes of computation, a radius gap without an attaining witness, or a verified finite outcome. Do not infer an impossibility outside the enumerated alphabet/domain.
evidence: Complete radius-four coset pairing on all 4096 labeled K and a separate truth-table shorter-word exclusion agree: histogram [1,12,66,220,495,810,1017,922,529,24], maximum minimum 9, feedback gains 0. Restricted witnesses are replayed on all 128 dirty inputs for every K.

open_questions.first_step: Find one explicit K and a fully restored unrestricted word beating a certified restricted lower bound; use the coset method only in a bounded exclusion.
open_questions.blocked_by: No shorter candidate is known here; larger balls grow quickly. This result does not justify unbounded enumeration, and any candidate still needs precision/frame/hosting accounting.

optimistic_full_cost_budget: Every ordered single-source XOR costs one, including preparation and restoration. No allocations, COPY/ERASE, frame changes, recursive calls or free basis changes. A positive result would require a strictly shorter unrestricted witness with an exact restricted lower bound.
